This gives $s(112896s-61152)=0$, so $s=\frac{13}{24}$.

$$C_2 = \left(\tfrac{143}{21},\, \tfrac{65\sqrt3}{21}\right)$$

## Side lengths of $A_2B_2C_2$

$$|A_2B_2|^2=\left(\tfrac{64}{7}\right)^2+\left(\tfrac{16\sqrt3}{21}\right)^2=\tfrac{12544}{147}=\tfrac{256}{3}\implies |A_2B_2|=\tfrac{16}{\sqrt3}$$
$$|B_2C_2|^2=7^2+\left(\tfrac{7\sqrt3}{3}\right)^2=\tfrac{196}{3}\implies |B_2C_2|=\tfrac{14}{\sqrt3}$$
$$|C_2A_2|^2=\left(\tfrac{15}{7}\right)^2+\left(\tfrac{65\sqrt3}{21}\right)^2=\tfrac{4900}{147}=\tfrac{100}{3}\implies |C_2A_2|=\tfrac{10}{\sqrt3}$$

**Direct area check**: $[A_2B_2C_2]=\frac{\sqrt3}{882}|{-4802+18850-2288}|=\frac{11760\sqrt3}{882}=\frac{40\sqrt3}{3}$. ✓

The construction depends only on the triangle's *shape* (angles and side ratios), not its size. Since $A_2B_2C_2\sim A_1B_1C_1$ with identical vertex roles, applying the same construction yields $A_3B_3C_3\sim A_2B_2C_2$ with the same ratio $\frac{1}{\sqrt3}$, and so on inductively.

The areas form a geometric series with common ratio $\frac{1}{3}$:
$$[A_iB_iC_i] = 40\sqrt3\cdot\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{i-1}$$

## Final computation

$$\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}[A_iB_iC_i]=40\sqrt3\cdot\frac{1}{1-\frac13}=40\sqrt3\cdot\frac32=60\sqrt3$$

$$\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}[A_iB_iC_i]\right)^2=(60\sqrt3)^2=3600\cdot 3=10800$$

$$\boxed{10800}$$
